title: Enforce tenant-scoped KMS keys and augment audit headers for data-residency routing
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers with strict data residency requirements asked for stronger guarantees that KMS keys and RBAC bindings cannot be scoped across tenant/regional boundaries. This PR adds enforcement for tenant-scoped KMS usage, enriches audit headers with residency tags, and wires a runtime guard that rejects cross-region key references. High level changes: 1) new RBAC v2 policy fragment that constrains kms:Encrypt/Decrypt to tenant-owned keys and region-scoped aliases; 2) audit middleware that injects 'x-redwood-residency' and 'x-redwood-kms-scope' headers into audit events for downstream retention/alerting; 3) installer/helm checks to validate KMS alias patterns during Private install; 4) integration tests and docs. Backwards compatibility: default behaviour remains unchanged for customers who do not opt into tenancy-scoped keys; feature is gated behind a cluster-level flag 'enforceTenantKmsScope' and will be rolled out via canary. Checklist: [x] policy yaml + unit tests, [x] middleware and log enrichment, [x] helm value guard, [x] integration tests, [x] docs and runbook, [x] Linear/Jira linkage. Rollout plan: enable in staging for 48h, run smoke + residency regression suite, enable on selected Dedicated tenants, then opt-in for Private installs. Related: ENG-8672 implements telemetry for residency mismatches. Note: this description is one continuous string and includes the context, changes, and rollout notes.

summary_changes: Adds tenant-scoped KMS RBAC fragment, audit header enrichment for residency, helm/installer preflight KMS alias validation, integration tests, and ops docs. Feature gated by enforceTenantKmsScope.
release_notes: Security: Enforce tenant-scoped KMS key usage when enforceTenantKmsScope is enabled. Audit events now include x-redwood-residency and x-redwood-kms-scope to aid compliance and monitoring. Helm/installer will validate KMS alias patterns on Private installs. Backwards compatible when feature flag is disabled.
regulatory_context: Addresses customer requests for cryptographic boundary enforcement to meet regional data residency controls and auditors' requirements for key scoping and traceable audit artifacts.
manual_steps_for_ops: 1) Enable feature flag enforceTenantKmsScope=false by default. 2) Follow canary rollout: enable for staging tenants and run residency regression suite. 3) If residency mismatches occur, check metric audit.residency.mismatch and run provided remediation script scripts/ops/fix_kms_aliases.sh. 4) For Private installs, helm will fail preflight if alias pattern doesn't match the tenant scope.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: No automatic key rewriting. Existing clusters that rely on cross-tenant aliases will continue to work until the flag is enabled. Operators should notify customers before toggling the flag. Migration docs included.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives if tenant metadata is missing from older audit logs. Mitigation: shipping a fallback 'unknown-tenant' path and a migration tool to backfill tenant metadata. Also guarded by canary rollout and opt-in for Private installs.
